claim: The FemtoRV open-source RISC-V soft-core teaching project targets a hardware cost of about $40 per student and its smallest RV32I variant (quark) is implemented in roughly 400 lines of documented Verilog (about 100 lines without comments).
stance_target: low-cost, low-code-footprint feasibility of student RISC-V core projects
quoted_support: Mission statement: create teaching material for FPGAs, processor design and RISC-V, using around $40 per students... The most elementary version (quark), an RV32I core, weights 400 lines of VERILOG (documented version), and 100 lines if you remove the comments.

claim: The learn-fpga repository provides a structured two-episode tutorial that teaches building a RISC-V processor incrementally, from a blinking-LED design to a fully functional pipelined RISC-V core with graphics output.
stance_target: existence of structured, documented pedagogical pathways for RISC-V final-year projects
quoted_support: In Episode I, you will learn to build your own RISC-V processor, step by step, starting from the simplest design (that blinks a LED), to a fully functional RISC-V core that can compute and display graphics. In Episode II, you will learn how to design a pipelined processor.
